subject.title: [Bug] Telegram exec approval bubble not dismissed after clicking approve

question: Should maintainers replace the stale conflicting fork PR with a fresh narrow OpenClaw fix for this issue, or keep waiting on/adopting that fork branch?
rationale: Automation should not queue a duplicate fix while an open closing PR is still linked, but the linked fork PR is conflicting, uneditable by maintainers, and targets the removed handler path.

options.title: Replace with a fresh active-runtime fix
options.body: Close or ignore the stale fork candidate and land a new narrow fix against `extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.ts` with Telegram proof.

options.title: Adopt and rework the fork branch
options.body: A maintainer can manually port the useful idea from the fork PR into the active runtime path if preserving that contribution is preferred.

options.title: Leave waiting on contributor
options.body: Keep the issue blocked on the fork PR author rebasing and retargeting the implementation, which may delay a narrow bug fix.

recommendation.title: Replace with a fresh active-runtime fix
recommendation.body: Close or ignore the stale fork candidate and land a new narrow fix against `extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.ts` with Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the active native approval lifecycle and are the strongest history signal for the correct owner boundary.
